clue.text: When TV is something worth having?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left' for 'when I left'
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: A riddle asking when a television counts as a prized possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable possession or resource.

clue.text: Service broadcast on behalf of church

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
for means on behalf of, as in acting for someone
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church service broadcast on someone's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' here is one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: The military aviation arm is one of the armed services.

clue.text: Almost endure eating American spread

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes the other inside it
almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to suffer is to endure

explanation.surface: Nearly putting up with an American food spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' sits at the end looking like a food spread, but it is the definition, a verb meaning to pervade.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffuse is to spread over or through something.

clue.text: Request support for middle eastern undertaking

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits below, so this piece goes after the other
the middle letter of the word eastern is wanted

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A request to back a Middle Eastern venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle eastern' looks like the region but takes the middle letter of EASTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a job or piece of work to be done.

clue.text: Tools for mending bridges

definitions.meaning: structures that reach across a river or gap

explanation.surface: A request for the right kit to repair bridges.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanners is the British word for wrenches, and anything that spans a gap is literally a spanner.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanners are the British name for wrenches, and a bridge is literally one that spans.

clue.text: Mean to send ruler cards for being stationary too long

parts.note: par is the average or mean level
a king is a ruler
tickets are small printed cards

explanation.surface: Meaning to send a monarch some cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to send' is a link; the definition is what a motorist gets for overstaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Penalty notices are issued to motorists who overstay their parking time.

clue.text: No empty benefits for the upper classes

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word is removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: No more welfare handouts for the rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobs is British slang for wealthy, upper-class people.

clue.text: "But no one is up!" that's an excuse?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: save means but, as in all save one
no as written plus one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Claiming nobody is awake as a way to dodge something.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'is up', turns each piece where it stands, so the first gives EVAS and the second ION; the exclamation marks are only surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasion is a dodge or pretext used to avoid something.

clue.text: Pike, and how to kill it?

definitions.meaning: a pike is a long pointed weapon
to kill a pike fish you might impale it with a pointed shaft

explanation.surface: A fisherman asking how to kill a pike.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a pike-like weapon, and spearing is how one might kill a fish.

clue.text: Show desperation when chickens are at the corn!

definitions.meaning: to grasp at any hope, however weak
a clutch is a brood of chicks, and straws are corn stalks

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene of hens pecking at the grain.
explanation.walkthrough: A clutch is a set of eggs or chicks; corn stalks are straws.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means trying anything in a hopeless situation, and literally a brood at corn stalks.

clue.text: Judge America left in denial

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game
USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A judge leaving America ends up turning someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a denial of a request.

clue.text: Vital container

parts.note: read as an essential box, but vital also means relating to the vital organs, so this holds heart and lungs

explanation.surface: Describing a box you cannot do without.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony cage of the chest encloses and protects the heart and lungs, the vital organs.

clue.text: Love students to achieve responsibility

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: Love helping students take on responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK's main student body.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty resting on someone.

clue.text: Cartoon that's a tease

definitions.meaning: a comic ... is a row of cartoon drawings
a striptease, often called just a ..., is a teasing undressing act

explanation.surface: Describing a cartoon as something that teases.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip is a cartoon, and a strip show is a striptease.

clue.text: Sea legs always found here

parts.note: sea legs usually means a sailor's balance, but here it is the supports standing in the water under a seaside structure

explanation.surface: Where sailors never lose their balance on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside promenade jetty stands on legs planted in the sea.

clue.text: Brothers in law?

explanation.surface: Asking whether siblings could be in-laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks form a religious order, and order also means lawful peace.

clue.text: Government department the first to impose

parts.note: the FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department
1st, written IST, is short for first

explanation.surface: A government department being the first to impose a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The FO was the UK's Foreign Office; 1st is read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: To foist something is to force it on someone unwillingly.

clue.text: Prepare to empty lords, say

definitions.meaning: to get things ready for a fresh start
Lord's is a cricket stadium, so emptying it would mean vacating a sports venue

explanation.surface: Getting ready to evict the peers from the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a famous cricket ground in London; the clue drops the apostrophe so it reads as the peers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to remove obstacles before starting, and literally to empty a sports venue.

clue.text: Scraps are a bargain, dearies

parts.note: a snip is British slang for a bargain
pets are darlings, used as endearments

explanation.surface: A market trader telling customers that scraps are a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Snippets are small pieces or fragments.

clue.text: The scientist who developed internet is able

indicators.note: developed suggests something worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crediting a clever scientist with inventing the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges INTERNET IS ABLE into the physicist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein was the physicist behind relativity.

clue.text: Articles in France and Germany may be clean

parts.note: la and un are French articles, the and a
der is a German article meaning the

explanation.surface: Foreign articles might be cleaned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles in France and Germany' gives LA and UN (French) and DER (German).
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash clothes.

clue.text: Greeting bishop in departure for show

indicators.note: in means these pieces are put inside the other

parts.note: an exit is a departure
hi is a greeting
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop waving goodbye as he leaves a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit is to display or show.

clue.text: Firm riding for a takeover

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a jockey riding a horse is said to be up

explanation.surface: A company on horseback heading for a takeover bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden seizure of power.

clue.text: Organization encountered a body in space

parts.note: CO is short for company, an organization
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A company meeting a celestial body.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy object orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Ante-post?

definitions.meaning: an ante is a gambler's wager placed in advance
a post is a wooden pole driven into the ground

explanation.surface: Ante-post is a betting term for a wager placed well before a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated betting phrase splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is both a bet and a pointed wooden pole.

clue.text: Work on quiet retail outlet

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: sh is the sound used to call for quiet
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Working on a quiet store.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop is a store selling goods to the public.

clue.text: A heavy drinker may achieve nothing

parts.note: to win is to achieve or gain
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A drunk may achieve nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a habitual drinker of cheap wine.

clue.text: Cut to second point

parts.note: the nub is the central point

explanation.surface: Getting to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them.

clue.text: Forced terrorists for island

parts.note: made means compelled, as in made to do it
IRA, the Irish Republican Army, is the usual crossword terrorist group

explanation.surface: Terrorists forced to go to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic.

clue.text: Less than a full team having enough strength to be valid

parts.note: a cricket or football team has eleven, so one short leaves ten
able means having the power or capacity

explanation.surface: A team one player short still strong enough to hold its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable argument is defensible and sound.

clue.text: A slow one to rise to dress

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or set in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone slow getting up to put on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like clothing but means arrange, rearranging TO RISE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile is proverbially slow, as in the fable of the hare.

clue.text: Mad about hotel pools

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone crazy about hotel swimming pools.
explanation.definitionFit: Public baths are swimming pools.
